newsitem.title: GERMANY: German December jobless rises to 4.156 million.
newsitem.headline: German December jobless rises to 4.156 million.

text.p: German unemployment rose to a seasonally adjusted 4.156 million in December, a new post-war record, the Federal Labour Office said on Thursday.
The unemployment rate, which is based on unadjusted data, rose to 10.8 percent from 10.3 percent in November. The number of unemployed workers rose by 48,000 from last month.
Independent analysts had expected a rise of between 35,000 and 60,000 from November's record 4.1 million unemployed on an adjusted basis.

In western Germany, the number of people out of work on a seasonally adjusted basis rose to 2.948 million in December, or by 22,000 from the month before. Eastern Germany added 26,000 to its unemployment rolls, with the total number of jobless rising to 1.208 million in December.
On an unadjusted basis, the number of Germans out of work rose to 4.148 million in December from 3.942 million in November.

The data reaffirmed views that the country's jobs crisis has intensified. Germany's DGB trade union federation warned this week that December unemployment data on an unadjusted basis would rise to 4.1 million before temporarily climbing to between 4.5 and 4.6 million by February due to the cold winter.
